keySentence: The jungle's law is absolute — those who break it are cast out from the community.

facts.Page story text 1 (draft, teacher check: Shere Khan the tiger thought he was above the Law. He hunted wherever he wanted and threatened other animals. The wolf pack grew angry at his arrogance and his rudeness. Akela the leader warned him that the Law had no exceptions. Even the strongest animal had to follow the shared rules. When Shere Khan ignored this warning the pack turned against him. The jungle's law is absolute — those who break it are cast out from the community.
facts.Page story text 2 (draft, teacher check: Shere Khan the tiger believed that he was above the Law of the Jungle entirely. He hunted where he pleased and threatened animals who were under the pack's protection. The wolf pack grew increasingly angry at his arrogance and his complete disregard for order. Akela the lead wolf warned him that the Law applied to every creature without any exception. Even the strongest and most feared animal in the jungle had to answer to the common rules. When Shere Khan ignored the warning the pack began to turn against him one by one. A community cannot survive when its strongest members refuse to be bound by its shared rules. The jungle's law is absolute — those who break it are cast out from the community.
facts.Page story text 3 (draft, teacher check: Shere Khan the great Bengal tiger carried himself as though the Law of the Jungle had been written for lesser creatures than himself. He hunted in forbidden territory, threatened cubs, and mocked the wolf pack openly whenever their elders tried to correct his behavior. Akela, the old leader of the Seeonee wolf pack, was the first to speak plainly about what was happening inside their territory. He reminded Shere Khan that the Law made no distinction between the weak and the strong, the young and the old, the feared and the unfeared. Every creature, the Law said, was bound by it — and any creature who refused to be bound by it would eventually find itself without a community. Shere Khan laughed at this warning, as he laughed at most warnings, and he continued to behave exactly as he pleased. But the jungle began to grow cold around him in a way he had not expected — conversations stopped when he approached, and former allies drifted away. This is what happens, the Law teaches, to anyone who imagines themselves larger than the rules that hold their community together. The jungle's law is absolute — those who break it are cast out from the community.
